item.title: Inside Sweden: Prospective citizens' passports are held hostage by long waiting times
item.description: In this week's Inside Sweden newsletter The Local's Deputy Editor Becky Waterton explains the problems that arise when Swedish authorities hold on to your passport and residency cards when applying for citizenship.

item.title: EU to ink long-awaited trade deal with South American bloc
item.description: The European Union will on Saturday sign a deal 25 years in the making with the South American trade bloc Mercosur, creating one of the world's largest free trade areas at a time of growing protectionism and volatility.

item.title: Why are young Europeans increasingly supporting anti-immigration parties?
item.description: Younger voters across Europe are increasingly tempted by hard-right and anti-migrant parties, but experts say this can't be explained by anti-immigration politics alone.

item.title: TELL US: What Swedish food habits have you adopted as your own?
item.description: From forgetting the top slice in sandwiches to putting banana on pizzas, Swedes have some peculiar food habits. We want to hear from readers which habits they've ended up adopting and which they are still resisting. Tell us in the survey below.

item.title: What are my rights while I wait for my Swedish residence permit to be extended?
item.description: Many foreigners living in Sweden need to have a residence permit to live in the country legally. Permits are generally issued for two years at a time and can be renewed 30 days before expiry, at the earliest. But just what are your rights while you wait to hear back?

item.title: European leaders denounce Trump's tariff threats over Greenland
item.description: European leaders on Sunday hit back at US President Donald Trump's threat of tariffs over their opposition to his designs on Greenland, with far-right Italian leader Giorgia Meloni urging Washington against making a "mistake".

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Swedish PM replies to new tariff threat, Swedish military still in Greenland, support for Sweden Democrats and Social Democrats low among young people and more news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: What is the EU's anti-coercion 'bazooka' it could use against US?
item.description: Calls are growing louder for the European Union to deploy its powerful "anti-coercion instrument" in response to US President Donald Trump's threats to impose tariffs in the standoff over Greenland.

item.title: Swedish Liberal party calls for new agency to handle work permits
item.description: Johan Britz, Sweden's Labour market minister, has called for a new government agency specifically for handling work permit applications and at the same time blamed the government's harsh immigration rhetoric for deterring highly skilled workers.

item.title: Is Swedish media opinion starting to shift on migration?
item.description: This time last year was a frustrating time to cover Sweden's immigration crackdown, as sweeping moves to tighten rules were ignored by the Swedish media. A year on, the deportation of gainfully employed, well-integrated immigrants is a big story.
